hookSay: What if your AI assistant was truly yours? Open, portable, and built by you.

beats.label: The shift
beats.say: Engineering is changing. {AI|A I} agents now read code, run tools, and draft documentation. But most of them live on closed platforms.

beats.label: The stack
beats.say: In this workshop, you build your own harness from free and open source parts: {OpenCode|Open Code}, its plugins, open models you can run locally, Git, and documentation.

beats.label: Language-agnostic
beats.say: It is not tied to one language. Python, JavaScript, Java, {C++|C plus plus}, Go, or Rust: your workbench adapts to your project.

beats.label: Model Context Protocol
beats.say: Connect it to files, databases, {APIs|A P Is}, and your own scripts through the Model Context Protocol, with only the access you approve.

beats.label: Reusable skills
beats.say: Write reusable skills for code generation, review, testing, documentation, and research.

beats.label: Graph engineering
beats.say: Use graph tools to map a codebase: its modules, dependencies, and how everything connects.

beats.label: Research in the AI era
beats.say: Research is shifting too. Agents search the literature, summarise papers with citations, rerun experiments, and help draft in {LaTeX|lay-tek}. You still check every claim.

beats.label: What you take home
beats.say: You leave with a portable, documented workbench, reusable skills, and at least one custom {MCP|M C P} or automation of your own.

beats.label: Who it's for
beats.say: For undergraduates, engineers, and faculty. Use it for projects, hackathons, internships, research, and open source.

outro: The {AI|A I} Workbench Workshop. Build your own harness.

end.title: AI Workbench Workshop
end.subtitle: Build Your Own Harness
end.small: 100% free and open source stack · no proprietary platform needed
